label: sec:incompleteness-horizon-intro
html: The phase-transition boundary of the previous section constitutes a specific degree-0 opacity. We now establish that Goedel's diagonal argument, applied to the Skein Turing machine, forces any such opacity. The Proposition: Turing completeness with \mathbb{N}-embedding implies non-empty computational horizon constructs a non-computable function d(n) = \mathrm{eval}(e(n))(n) + 1 over the Skein resolution system. This witnesses a section of A_0 outside the reach of any finite braid. Remark: Incompleteness as degree-0 opacity: the Turing--Goedel--horizon triangle interprets the diagonal as a degree-0 vanishing locus. Remark: Statistical mechanics as the polynomial observable subcategory confines the framework to the polynomial-bandwidth observables of \S 1. Remark: The information paradox as a theorem of arithmetic concludes by equating the black-hole information paradox with Goedel incompleteness operating on Hawking quanta. The next section, Horizons and Aeons, adopts the computational horizon as the prototype for every jet horizon in the descended universe.
